newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Senate chief unsure about Colston probe.
newsitem.headline: Australian Senate chief unsure about Colston probe.

text.p: Australian Senate President Margaret Reid on Tuesday denied newspaper reports that she break ranks with her Liberal Party to propose a parliamentary inquiry into fraud allegations against key independent Mal Colston.
"That is highly speculative," a spokesman from Reid's office told Reuters, adding that Reid had made no decision on how she would handle the matter.

The Labor Opposition has repeatedly called for a Senate inquiry to investigate whether Colston had lied to the upper house of parliament when he blamed his former office manager, Christine Smith, for errors in his travel allowance claims.
Earlier this month, Smith recanted a statement that she was responsible for the errors, prompting Prime Minister John Howard to ask police to include the matter in their investigations.
Howard on Monday rejected calls for an immediate Senate inquiry on the grounds that it could prejudice police investigations.
Police were already investigating fraud allegations against Colston, who defected from the Labor opposition in August last year and whose vote is crucial to the passage of government legislation.
The senator has denied any wrongdoing.
Reid's spokesman said the only decision the Senate president had to make was whether dealing with the matter took precedence over other legislative duties when the Senate resumed on May 6.
"It's all very speculative to say she's decided one way or another," he said.
"She's the only person who knows that and it's something that she would keep to herself until such time as the Senate meets."
The government and opposition parties have demanded that Colston resign from his post as Senate deputy president.
Colston has so far refused to budge. He told Reid he would discuss his future with her sometime this week, but the spokesman said he was still to make contact with the president.
"He hasn't been in contact with us and that's one thing I can be quite categorical about," he said.
"He indicated in a message to the president that he was going to contact her this week,so that's what we're waiting on."
Colston was released from a Brisbane hospital last week after suffering an unspecified medical condition. He is currently convalescing in an undisclosed location.
